name: energy
source: Profile energy, with a project band of +4%. Dutch average needs: Gezondheidsraad 2022/19

name: protein
source: Profile g/kg x weight. Dutch norm for adults 0.83 g/kg: Gezondheidsraad 2021/10

name: fibre
source: Gezondheidsraad 2026/14: recommended range 3.0-3.5 g/MJ (2006: 3.4). The model uses the low end as its minimum

name: carbs
source: Gezondheidsraad 2026/14 gives no number (2001: at least 40 en%): mainly wholegrain, vegetables, fruit, pulses, dairy

name: fat
source: Gezondheidsraad 2026/14: 20-40 en%, unchanged from 2001

name: satfat
source: Gezondheidsraad 2026/14: as low as possible, with 10 en% as an intermediate step

name: trans
source: Gezondheidsraad 2026/14: as low as possible, no number. The model keeps 1 en% (the 2001 limit) as a working maximum

name: linoleic
source: Gezondheidsraad 2026/14: AI 4 en% (was 2 en% since 2001)

name: ala
source: Gezondheidsraad 2026/14: AI 0.5 en% (was 1 en% since 2001)

name: epa_dha
source: Gezondheidsraad 2026/14: AI 200 mg/day for adults, unchanged

name: sodium
source: Gezondheidsraad 2015/24 and 2025/19: at most 6 g salt. WHO and EFSA 2019 use 2000 mg sodium

name: potassium
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: AI 3500 mg, adults

name: calcium
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: 950 mg at 25-69 (18-24: 1000; women 50-69: 1100; from 70: 1200). Upper limit 2500: EFSA 2012

name: phosphorus
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: AI 550 mg, listed as too little data for a good norm and not meant as a target

name: magnesium
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: AI men 350, women 300 mg

name: iron_abs
source: Voedingscentrum 2025 iron (men 11, women 18-49 16 mg) x EFSA 2015 absorption (men 16%, premenopausal women 18%). Haem 25% and non-haem 10% are a model rule

name: iron
source: EFSA 2024: safe level 40 mg, not a formal upper limit. Taken over by Voedingscentrum 2025

name: zinc
source: EFSA 2014 at 900 mg/day phytate: men 14.0, women 11.0 mg, chosen for this diet. The Dutch norm is lower: men 9.0, women 7.0 (Voedingscentrum 2025). Upper limit 25: EFSA

name: copper
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: 0.9 mg. Upper limit 5 mg: EFSA. EFSA 2023 also has an ADI of 0.07 mg/kg, 4.4 mg at 62.5 kg

name: iodine
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: AI 150 µg. Upper limit 600 µg: EFSA

name: selenium
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: AI 70 µg. Upper limit 255 µg: EFSA 2023. Gezondheidsraad 2024 revised how this norm is qualified, not the number

name: vitA
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: ADH men 800, women 690 µg RAE

name: retinol
source: EFSA 2024: upper limit 3000 µg preformed vitamin A

name: thiamin
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: ADH 0.1 mg/MJ

name: riboflavin
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: 1.6 mg at 18-69

name: niacin
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: ADH 1.6 mg NE/MJ

name: vitB6
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: 1.5 mg (men from 51: 1.8). Upper limit 12 mg: EFSA 2023

name: folate
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: 300 µg DFE

name: folic_acid
source: EFSA 2023: upper limit 1000 µg, for added folic acid and similar forms only

name: vitB12
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: 2.8 µg

name: vitC
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: 75 mg

name: vitD
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: 10 µg at 18-69 (from 70: 20). Upper limit 100 µg: EFSA 2023

name: vitE
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: AI men 13, women 11 mg, listed as too little data for a good norm and not meant as a target. Upper limit 300 mg: EFSA, under review

name: vitK1
source: Voedingscentrum 2025: AI 70 µg

name: histidine
source: WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 (TRS 935), table 23: 10 mg/kg/day

name: isoleucine
source: WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 (TRS 935), table 23: 20 mg/kg/day

name: leucine
source: WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 (TRS 935), table 23: 39 mg/kg/day

name: lysine
source: WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 (TRS 935), table 23: 30 mg/kg/day

name: met_cys
source: WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 (TRS 935), table 23: 15 mg/kg/day

name: phe_tyr
source: WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 (TRS 935), table 23: 25 mg/kg/day

name: threonine
source: WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 (TRS 935), table 23: 15 mg/kg/day

name: tryptophan
source: WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 (TRS 935), table 23: 4 mg/kg/day

name: valine
source: WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 (TRS 935), table 23: 26 mg/kg/day

name: free_sugars
source: WHO 2015: below 10 en% (strong), below 5 en% (conditional). Gezondheidsraad 2026/14: as low as possible, with 10 en% as an intermediate step
